newsitem.title: USA: Conservative group offers U.S. budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Conservative group offers U.S. budget plan.

text.p: The Heritage Foundation Thursday said it offered a proposal to balance the federal budget by 2002 that would slow the growth of federal spending and provide a tax cut.

The 450-page plan calls $108 billion in savings from the Medicare health care program for the elderly through 2002. It also calls for a 0.7 percentage point downward adjustment in the consumer price index, a change called for by the Boskin Commission to bring the index in line with true price changes.

The conservative think tank also recommended a five-year $193 billion tax cut. It would include a $500 per child tax credit, would cut the capital gains tax rate in half, expand individual retirement accounts, and set up tax-free savings accounts for college tuition.

The group said its plan would slow the growth of federal spending by $510 billion over the next five years. Under its proposal federal spending will rise $176 billion during the period while tax revenue collections will go up by $300 billion.

Several federal programs were recommended for termination including the Rural Electrification Administration. The group recommended consolidation of the many federal job training programs and elimination of many federal subsidies to business including the $62,000 a year paid to unify international wine standards.
